en: So finally, let's get started writing some
code. And for this, I'm in a brand new empty
project, empty folder opened up here in
Visual Studio Code.
And I'll start by creating a Python project
by running uv init using the UV Python
project and package manager. Now UV is a
tool you
won't have on your system by default, but
you can install it on all operating systems.
Attached, you find a link to the official
installation installation instructions. And
the great thing about this
uvtool is not just that it's free to use,
but that it's an extremely capable Python
package and project manager.
It'll automatically create and manage a
virtual Python environment on a per-project
basis, ensuring that any third-party
dependencies you install
don't pollute your global Python
installation. It's extremely fast and
overall just an amazing tool.
Therefore, as mentioned, attached you find a
link to the installation instructions for
macOS and Windows. And once you got that
tool installed, you should be able to run
uvinit to create a new Python project.
Of course, you can also create a Python
project in any other way you want though,
because we won't really use any more
advanced UV features. We just need a Python
project here.
So out of the box here, I got a project with
a bunch of files, most importantly, a
main.py file, which is pretty empty
initially.
And I'll use this file as a foundation now
to build a first basic AI-powered workflow.
